facts.text: The musk duck gets its common name from the peculiar musky smell it gives off during the breeding season.
facts.quote: This animal derives its common name from the peculiar musky odour it emanates during the breeding season.

facts.text: A male musk duck has a distinctive large, leathery lobe under its bill, which swells during the breeding season.
facts.quote: Adult males are 60 to 70 cm (24 to 28 in) long and have a distinctive large, leathery lobe underneath the bill

facts.text: Musk ducks float very low in the water, almost like a cormorant, with their large webbed feet set well back on the body.
facts.quote: Musk ducks float very low in the water, almost like a cormorant, and the large, webbed feet are well back on the body.

facts.text: During breeding season, males advertise with a splash, two soft calls, a loud whistle and a deep grunt, repeated every 4 or 5 seconds for up to half an hour.
facts.quote: then two soft, sharp cuc cuc calls; then a loud whistle and a deep grunt. This sequence can be started at any time of day or night, with or without an associated visual display, and repeated every 4 or 5 seconds for as long as half an hour at a time.

facts.text: In 1987 a musk duck named Ripper at Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve was recorded apparently mimicking human speech, saying "you bloody fool".
facts.quote: a rediscovered tape that originally was recorded in 1987 of a musk duck named Ripper at Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve in the Australian Capital Territory, who appeared to be the first duck recorded to  mimic human speech

facts.text: The male musk duck plays no part in building the nest or raising the young.
facts.quote: The male plays no part in building the nest or raising the young.

facts.text: Musk ducks rarely fly and are awkward on land, but when needed they fly swiftly for long distances with rapid, shallow wing beats.
facts.quote: However, at need musk ducks fly swiftly and for long distances, with rapid, shallow wing beats.

facts.text: Musk ducks stay on the water at night, sleeping well out from land with the head tucked into the body or under a wing.
facts.quote: They stay on the water at night, sleeping well out from land with the head tucked into the body or under a wing.

facts.text: A female musk duck slips quietly into the water and submerges when leaving the nest to feed, not surfacing until she is well away from it.
facts.quote: When leaving the nest to feed, she slips quietly into the water and submerges, not surfacing until she is well away from it.
